q: Echoes are produced where a sound wave is reflected from a _____ surface.
e: Echoes come from reflection at a large hard surface. An echo is a repetition of the original sound. Soft porous surfaces swallow sound instead of echoing.

q: An echo is a repetition of sound due to the _____ of sound.
e: Echoes follow the laws of reflection: angle in equals angle out. A large hard wall sends a countable repeat; many walls make reverberation. An echo is reflection, not refraction.

q: The echo can be heard separately from the original sound if the source is much closer to the observer than to the _____ surface.
e: In Doppler formulas, fo is what the observer hears and vo is the observer's speed. Plus vo is toward the source, which raises frequency. You hear a separate echo when you sit closer to the source than to the reflector.

q: Reflection of sound obeys the laws of _____.
e: Echoes follow the laws of reflection: angle in equals angle out. A large hard wall sends a countable repeat; many walls make reverberation. An echo is reflection, not refraction. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum.

q: To reduce the effect of echo in buildings, walls are covered up with padding to _____ the incident sound.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Room treatment absorbs incident sound to kill echo.

q: Some animals such as bats are known to use _____ to navigate and locate their prey.
e: Echolocation means emitting sounds and reading the returning echoes. Bats navigate and hunt that way. A bat's own shout-and-listen is echolocation; sonar is the engineered analogue.

q: Echolocation is the special ability of emitting sounds and interpreting the _____.
e: Echolocation means emitting sounds and reading the returning echoes. Bats navigate and hunt that way. Sonar is the engineered version in water. Special ability of emitting sounds and interpreting cannot be dropped from this process without changing the law.

q: A _____ is a reflection of light or sound waves, or a wide reaching impact of an action.
e: Diffraction is bending around an obstacle or through a hole into the geometrical shadow. It is obvious when the opening is comparable to the wavelength. Half-integer path is out of phase, not a resonance label.

q: To reduce the effect of echo, floors are covered with rugs and carpets which _____ the incident sound.
e: Sound is a longitudinal pressure wave in a compressible medium. It is not electromagnetic, so it cannot cross vacuum. Room treatment absorbs incident sound to kill echo. Range follows from the go-and-return time, v = 2d/t.
